posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
How does one calculate the percentage alcohol to water using the specific gravity number.

Example;

What is the percentage of ISO alcohol to water if the liquid has a specific gravity of .86?

Isopropyl Alcohol has a specific gravity of .785 at 20C.

Thank you in advance!

posts.author: Ed Wesly
posts.content_md:
Specific gravity of a material compares the density of that material to the density of water. Water has a specific gravity of 1.0. 

The density of water is a kilogram per liter. Anything with a specific gravity < 1 will float, > 1 will sink. I would see specific gravity listed on the industrial sized cans of tomato sauce when I worked in a pizza place in high school, I guess to show how much the sauce was or wasn't watered down.

To solve your problem, let x = percent of alcohol in solution. Then (1 - x) is the amount of water. .786 is specific gravity of the alcohol.

.786x + 1.0(1-x) = .86

.786x + 1 -x = .86

-.215x = -.14

x = .651 or 65%

Alternatively, letting x = % of H2O

x + .785(1-x) = .86

.215x = .860 - .785

.215x = .075

x = .348 or 35%

I was trained as a math teacher and that is still one of the things I have to do to put the chops on the table!

How do you measure the specific gravity?

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md:
> **Ed Wesly:** How do you measure the specific gravity?

When I was homebrewing I used a hydrometer, but I just realized that a more direct (and possibly more accurate) method would be to measure out 100 ml or so and weigh it. An S.G. of 0.95 would weigh 95 grams and so on.

I realize that this is excruciatingly obvious, but it struck me as something possibly of use to someone stranded on a desert island with a digital scale and graduated beaker, but no hydrometer

posts.content_md:
> **Ed Wesly:** x = .651 or 65%Alternatively, letting x = % of H2Ox = .348 or 35%

So you would take your hidrometer reading and multiply it by .651 to get the percentage of Alcohol or multipuly it by .348 to get the percentage of water.

> **Ed Wesly:** How do you measure the specific gravity?

In order to measure the specific gravity of a solution lighter than water you will want to but a distillers hydrometer. It is a glass bulb with lead shot. It is calabrated to displace a measured amount of fluid and give you a reading on a scale.

A pycnometer is about 100 times more accurate than a hydrometer. Not needed for holography but it helps in my work. I used one while visiting UC Davis but I have never had one to use for real. It takes a very accurate scale.

Now really OT...

UC Davis has a really cool that has a small hollow U-tube in a vacuum. You fill the tube with your sample and hit a button. It sweeps the tube through a vibrating frequency in order to find the resonance frequency. Once the volume and the resonance frequency are known then the SG is very easy to calculate. The machine reads in about 10 seconds to 6 decimal places.
